title: can you please tell me exactly how many users are assigned to the agent russomic

content.text: can you please tell me exactly how many users are assigned to the agent russomichelle_47
I'll help you find how many users are assigned to agent russomichelle_47. Let me pull up the manual to find the exact function for that.{{READ:hierarchy_management}}

I need to find how many users are assigned to agent russomichelle_47. The `traverse_hierarchy` function will get me the children (assigned users) of this agent. Let me make that call.{{TOOL:traverse_hierarchy}}

The hierarchy traversal returned too much data. Let me try a different approach using the aggregation_reporting class to get a count directly, which should be more efficient.{{READ:aggregation_reporting}}

Perfect! The `generate_aggregation_report` function with `metric: "count"` and `target_ancestor_username` is exactly what I need. This will efficiently return just the count without dumping all user data.{{TOOL:generate_aggregation_report}}

Agent **russomichelle_47** has exactly **29 users** assigned to them.

This was retrieved using the aggregation report function which counts all USER-type accounts that have russomichelle_47 as their ancestor in the hierarchy.
mm nice, what about the agent wross_10
Let me check how many users are assigned to agent wross_10 using the same approach.{{READ:aggregation_reporting}}
Got it — I'll use the same `generate_aggregation_report` function with `metric: "count"` and `target_ancestor_username: "wross_10"` with a filter for USER type.{{TOOL:generate_aggregation_report}}
Agent **wross_10** has **35 users** assigned to them — that's 6 more than russomichelle_47.
can you give me 5 of those users assigned to russomichelle_47
Let me pull up the manual to find the right function for listing specific users in a hierarchy.{{READ:hierarchy_management}}

Perfect — I'll use `traverse_hierarchy` with `direction: "children"` to get the users directly assigned to russomichelle_47. Since we want 5 users, I'll set `max_depth: 1` to get direct children only.{{TOOL:traverse_hierarchy}}
Let me try a different approach — I'll use `traverse_hierarchy` with a `limit` parameter to cap the results at 5 users.{{TOOL:traverse_hierarchy}}
Let me try narrowing this down further by specifying only the `username` field in `return_fields` to minimize data transfer.{{TOOL:traverse_hierarchy}}
Let me check the account_lookup manual — there might be a direct lookup function that can search for users by their parent/assignee.{{READ:account_lookup}}

I see — `lookup_account` can filter by any document field. If the hierarchy stores parent assignments as a field like `parent_username` or `assigned_to`, I can query directly. Let me try filtering by a likely field name.{{TOOL:lookup_account}}
That field didn't match. Let me try `assigned_to` as the field name.{{TOOL:lookup_account}}
That field also didn't match. Let me try `ancestor_username` or `manager_username` as common hierarchy field names.{{TOOL:lookup_account}}
That field also didn't match. Let me try `ancestor_username` or `parent` as alternative field names.{{TOOL:lookup_account}}

context_diary: Successfully used aggregation_reporting.generate_aggregation_report with parameters {"metric": "count", "target_ancestor_username": "wross_10", "filters": {"type": "USER"}} returning 35 users. Pattern confirmed: this function is the efficient method for count queries on hierarchy assignments, avoiding the data limit issues of hierarchy_management.traverse_hierarchy. russomichelle_47 has 29 users, wross_10 has 35 users.
